title: Scheme-base-change test of an algebraic-space property on a representable stack morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $F,G$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes, with morphisms and 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Let $f:F\to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $P$ be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$. Define $P(f)$ to mean: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $t:h_T\to G$, there exist an algebraic space $Z$, its projection $p:Z\to h_T$, and an equivalence $Z\simeq h_T\times_G F$ compatible up to 2-isomorphism with projection to $h_T$, such that $P(Z\to T)$. Here $T$ as an algebraic space is its representable fppf sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. For an algebraic space $W$ and $q:W\to G$, a presentation of the base change with projection is an algebraic space $V$, a map $p:V\to W$, and an equivalence $V\simeq W\times_G F$ whose composite with projection to $W$ is 2-isomorphic to $p$. This retains the actual 2-fibre-product map and imposes no source-chart test on $P$.
